task:
Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description

When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

Now the bug is clearly demonstrated. The custom site's `get_admin_url` returns "admin" (the model `__str__`), which means `NoReverseMatch` is raised and caught. This happens because:

1. The custom admin site's URL patterns are NOT registered in the URL configuration
2. Without `current_app`, `reverse('admin:auth_user_change', ...)` always resolves against the default admin site's URLs

The second test passes because both sites fail to resolve (both return plain text), so they're "equal" - but that's not the real test scenario. In the real scenario, the custom site has its own URL patterns registered, and without `current_app`, the reverse call would match the WRONG admin site's URLs.

The real-world scenario: When you register a custom admin site with its own URLs, and a model has a readonly FK field, the `get_admin_url` would generate a URL pointing to the default admin site instead of the custom one. This is exactly the bug described in the issue.

## Summary

**Bug**: When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed in a custom `AdminSite` and that ForeignKey is listed in `readonly_fields`, the URL generated for the link always points to `/admin/...` (the default admin site) instead of the custom admin site's URL prefix (e.g., `/custom-admin/...`).

**Root Cause**: In `django/contrib/admin/helpers.py:212`, the `get_admin_url` method on `AdminReadonlyField` called `reverse()` without passing `current_app`, so the URL resolution always matched the default `admin` namespace. Every other URL generation in the admin framework (e.g., `response_add`, `response_change`, `response_delete` in `options.py`) correctly passes `current_app=self.admin_site.name`.

**Fix**: Added `current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name` to the `reverse()` call in `get_admin_url` at `/testbed/django/contrib/admin/helpers.py:215`. This is a one-line change that makes the readonly field URL generation consistent with the rest of the admin framework.

- `reproduce_issue.py` - 2 tests pass (custom site generates `/custom_admin/` URLs)
- `edge_case_tests.py` - 7 tests pass (prefix, change view, PK, anchor tag, display, non-existent objects, multiple fields)
